name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.28.0 — prose-cap.js's entry regex is broadened from a bullet that must OPEN with a bracket tag (backtick-wrapped or bare) to any top-level `- ` bullet, closing a fail-open found 2026-08-23: real hosts write the `[host]`/`[plugin]` tag at the END of the entry, so Upwell's `.claude/rules/spec-pipeline.md` held 138 Gotchas entries of which 0 matched — the cap had never fired there and nothing was ever evicted — while this repo's own tag-first file kept the live-file suite test green (authored ≠ activated; second recorded member of the silent-matcher fail-open class after the AC-ID prefix-collision coverage fail-open of 2026-08-22). No doctrine ever mandated tag position; the new shape is the same top-level-bullet count the review driver's sidecar grammar and build.md's ledger count already use, indented continuation lines still never count, and overcounting only fires the cap early where a human judges at fold time. Same-day incident fix per core § Incident Policy: regex + script-header history, tag-at-end regression and deliberate-trip tests, specs/20260823/06's Contracts amended in place; spec-review-driver.js's strict flush-left sidecar grammar is deliberately untouched (JJ ruling 2026-08-23). 7.27.0 — the deviations sidecar (`<spec>.deviations.md`) moves from pure convention to backstop enforcement inside `spec-review-driver.js`'s existing machinery, closing specs/20260823/07: a skipped fold or a count-invisible entry now surfaces as a driver refusal with a named remedy, never a silent loss. (1) The driver validates the sidecar against a bullets-only entry grammar (blank / `#`-prefixed / `- ` bullet / indented continuation of an open entry; anything else is malformed) whenever it derives state, and persists the observation (`entries`, `malformed`) into the review sidecar on every derivation while the file exists on disk. (2) The CLOSE step's printed fold instruction now enumerates every entry (numbered, 120-char-bounded first line) ahead of the fold, so the folding session sees the full content in the instruction channel. (3) `--mark closed` gains two refusals, both exit 2 with a named remedy and state left unchanged: the sidecar still exists on disk (fold not done), or it was deleted but the last persisted observation records one or more malformed lines (restore-and-repair remedy naming `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`). No new review leg, script, or ledger field: fold outcome stays a session judgment, and the build row's `deviations` count remains the cross-spec signal. 7.26.0 — the two append-only prose surfaces this repo accreted without pruning (23 § Gotchas entries in 23 days; `.claude/agent-memory/` notes reviewed only when a diff happened to touch the note file itself) become self-pruning. (1) New `spec/scripts/prose-cap.js` caps the host rules' § Gotchas section at 15 entries, exit 1 naming the overage and the remedy; it runs at `/spec:review` CLOSE and at `/spec:escape` step 6 (appending at cap now requires naming an eviction first) and is pinned by this repo's own suite against its live `.claude/rules/spec-pipeline.md`, red on the pre-image (23 entries) and green only once the triage below lands. Eviction is a closed three-fate enum: delete (wrong, dead-cited, or mechanized), merge (durable engineering truth into `docs/canonical/{area}.md`), or mechanize (a recurring class becomes a script per core § Incident Policy). (2) New `spec/scripts/memory-sweep.js` widens `/spec:review` CLOSE's agent-memory disposal trigger from the diff touching the note file to the diff touching what the note is about — a path-shaped token in the note body intersecting the spec's changed set (diff-hit) — plus a TTL of 10 review-stage ledger rows postdating the note's last git commit (ttl-expired, oldest-first, at most 3 per run), with a `reviewed:` carry-reset. The sweep is deliberately never a verdict input — it exits 0 with or without findings — and this partially reopens specs/20260821/02 D10's no-memory-lint ruling on a second recorded false-memory incident (2026-08-23, a gate-scripts note falsified by the same diff that shipped it). (3) A one-time triage pays the standing debt down from 23 Gotchas entries to 10: 7 dead/duplicate/mechanized entries deleted, 6 durable Node/git/testing truths promoted into new `docs/canonical/scripts.md`.
